objects.title: Participation in everyday life
objects.statement: Explore frictions between what people value doing and what their environments let them do. Scope includes home, neighbourhood and social participation, with overlaps into care work and provision. Excludes a general catalogue of diseases or communication products. Boundaries remain revisable.

confidence.rationale: Editorial boundary informed by WHO context; not a validated universal taxonomy.

provenance.method: Scoped editorial curation, independently of company themes

objects.title: Continue activities that matter to me
objects.statement: Candidate aspiration to investigate in the person’s own terms: continue relationships and activities they value, with agency over help.

confidence.rationale: Requires field research; not an observed or verified claim.

provenance.method: Scoped editorial curation, independently of company themes

objects.title: Environments can obstruct valued activities
objects.statement: Physical and social environments can constrain what older people are able to do.

confidence.rationale: Supported at a broad global level by WHO; local mechanisms and distribution remain unresearched.

provenance.method: Scoped editorial curation, independently of company themes

objects.title: Fit between environments and capacity
objects.statement: WHO describes environments as affecting health through barriers and incentives and enabling valued activity despite capacity loss. This is a broad mechanism, not a measured local causal effect.

confidence.rationale: Institutional synthesis; no local causal estimate.

provenance.method: Scoped editorial curation, independently of company themes

objects.title: Difficulty initiating digital family contact
objects.statement: Candidate question: in which situations do digital interfaces obstruct family contact for an older person, and whose goal does contact serve?

confidence.rationale: Requires field research; not an observed or verified claim.

objects.title: Initiating a family call at home
objects.statement: Illustrative research scenario: a person wants to call family at a time they choose. No person, interview, quotation or frequency is asserted.

confidence.rationale: A prompt for fieldwork, not an observed day-in-the-life.

objects.title: Ask a relative to operate the interface
